note: What the factory requires and what each requirement says when it is empty (FR-23, t-305). `scripts/null_outcomes.py` walks the index rows that carry an item list, every stage's `required_outputs` and the tool fields the FR-11 walk selects, and demands exactly ONE home for each: a `null_outcome` declaration in the contract (the contract's own file), a `never_empty` row here (with its guard, or the reason none is needed), or a `pending` row here (the node of t-305 at which its declaration arrives). `pending` only shrinks: `ratchet` keeps its history, so a new required item cannot be born pending - it is declared, or given a never_empty row, in the commit that adds it. `default: true` marks a row the N0 default rule put at the node of its stage (`default_node_by_stage`) because the inventory named no other; `intent: never_empty` marks an item an empty plan can never legitimately empty (an empty S3/S4 plan is the open-questions halt, not a result, owner 02.10). `tightening_exceptions` are the scalars a later node's declaration will make refuse the word `none`, measured on the fixtures. `validator` rows are guards that live in validators and gates; the walk does not meet them, the detector pins their count. Never_empty rows say WHY an empty is never right; the guard column names a function resolved by AST in scripts/ (never a line number), or `no guard:` with the reason.

never_empty.requirement: one row per source of the story
never_empty.why: S1's scope is one row per source, and the story's own ticket is the `task` source the scout collects first; an S1 with no source row is a broken S0, not a result
never_empty.guard: no guard: handoff_check.py::check refuses the empty list (`no rows`), which is the intended outcome; the role's door is `blocked` and handoff_help.py

never_empty.requirement: one row per requirement of the register
never_empty.why: no requirement means no oracle (FR-58): an S2 with no R row is a story nobody has read, and a register with no R rows is refused again at delivery (traceability: nothing was traced)
never_empty.guard: no guard: handoff_check.py::check refuses the empty list (`no rows`), which is the intended outcome; the role's door is `blocked` and handoff_help.py

never_empty.requirement: one row per case of the author's window
never_empty.why: a window holds at least one case: the driver never opens one over an empty stage-scope; a window all of whose Then clauses are remainders of the plan still has its case rows and lists no tests, and says so (`no tests planned for this window`, E41)

never_empty.requirement: one row per case of the window the critic reviews
never_empty.why: the critic reviews the author's window, and that window is never opened empty

never_empty.requirement: one row per case the plan covers
never_empty.why: an S5 whose stage-scope is empty has no plan: not written, no automate cases, and S5 closes as it did before the plan existed (E7); a plan with no case row is a broken plan, and `check` names the missing cases

never_empty.requirement: one row per case the plan critic reviews
never_empty.why: the critic reviews a plan that exists only for a non-empty scope (NE25); the review of a plan with no remark is `approved` with `remarks: []`, which the contract declares in its own words, and its scope is never empty

never_empty.requirement: one row per instance or manual case the runner ran
never_empty.why: the runner is dispatched only with a non-empty stage-scope; an S6 with nothing to execute closes by code, and no form is written

never_empty.requirement: one row per failure the analyst triaged
never_empty.why: the analyst writes this form only for a triage, and a triage is dispatched only when something failed; an S7 with no failure closes by code and no scribe form is written - the read-only investigation that may run there hands back the `s7-analyst-to-automator` form with `scope: []` and writes no scribe form

never_empty.requirement: an inconclusive manual result carries at least one evidence ref
never_empty.why: an inconclusive with no evidence cannot be told from a check that was never attempted

never_empty.requirement: a bug draft carries manual steps
never_empty.why: a defect that cannot be stated as steps a person follows is not a bug; the null is no draft at all

never_empty.requirement: a coverage obligation names at least one requirement ref
never_empty.why: an obligation that traces to no requirement has no oracle behind it

never_empty.requirement: a decision to write or run a check names the check
never_empty.why: a decision to write a check that names no check is not a decision

never_empty.requirement: a manual record states what was actually seen
never_empty.why: "the page did not load" is an observation and never an empty one

never_empty.requirement: test-report.md and work/delivery-summary.json are on disk before gate B is shown
never_empty.why: S8 produces both before the gate is shown, so a gate with neither is a factory block

never_empty.requirement: the requirements register holds at least one R row
never_empty.why: no requirement row means nothing was traced, and a delivery over nothing is not ready

never_empty.requirement: the story's own state file exists
never_empty.why: the story's own state and journal in one file; a story without it has no stage to close
never_empty.guard: no guard: stage_done.py refuses to close any stage without it (`no pipeline.json ... S0 writes it`), so a missing file is a broken story and never a null

never_empty.requirement: the scout's manifest of what it collected
never_empty.why: the ticket is always a source (NE1's reason), so a manifest with nothing collected is a broken S1
never_empty.guard: no guard: the S1 form's empty scope is refused (NE1), and the scout's exit gate requires the file (stages.json required_outputs)

never_empty.requirement: the bundle context_bundle.py builds from the manifest
never_empty.why: built by code from the manifest (context_bundle.build) and always carries its skeleton; its content is empty only when the manifest is, which NE17 rules out
never_empty.guard: no guard: NE17 rules the empty manifest out, and the stage's exit gate requires the file

never_empty.requirement: the register holds at least one R row
never_empty.why: no R row means no oracle (the twin of NE15), and delivery refuses a register with none

never_empty.requirement: a readiness verdict with the open questions and their owners
never_empty.why: a readiness verdict is always a verdict; a story with none has not been read, and the witness gate holds a rule for the file
never_empty.guard: no guard: check_witness.py holds a rule for requirements-readiness.json at the role's exit, and a missing verdict is a halt, never a null

never_empty.requirement: the brief the person reads at gate A
never_empty.why: gate A shows the person this brief first among the paths, so a gate A with no brief cannot be shown
never_empty.guard: no guard: the stage's exit gate requires the file (stages.json required_outputs) and gate_brief.py lists it first among the paths

never_empty.requirement: the ledger ledger.py generates
never_empty.why: generated by ledger.py and never authored; a story with nothing executed still has a ledger with delivery_ready and its reasons
never_empty.guard: no guard: generated by ledger.py on every run, so there is no authored empty to refuse

never_empty.requirement: the readable form of the ledger
never_empty.why: written by the same generator as NE22 in the same call, so it exists whenever the ledger does
never_empty.guard: no guard: as NE22, the same ledger.py call writes both files

never_empty.requirement: the report the scribe writes and gate B reads
never_empty.why: gate B reads it, and the gate preflight refuses a gate whose report is not on disk

never_empty.requirement: a gate B decision states each order of gate B (bugs, mr) as due or not_ordered
never_empty.why: what a person decided at gate B is carried out by executors, and the empty outcome of an order is the status `not_ordered`, never a missing key; a decision that carries none is read as one recorded before the orders existed

never_empty.requirement: a finding line written by add or correct carries at least one evidence ref (a withdraw carries none, t-094 F-2)
never_empty.why: a finding no reader can open is a sentence, not a finding: the register holds only what a file under the task root shows; the empty outcome of the register itself is its absence (no target, no file, no report block)

never_empty.requirement: a pass carries a quote per Then of the request's thens, a fail at least one; an inconclusive, a request with `thens: {}` and a request made before the rule carry none
never_empty.why: a verdict that names no words of the captured text is a claim no reader can open; the empty outcomes are stated: an inconclusive stands on its limitation, an empty thens asks for nothing, and an old request is never refused for a rule it predates

never_empty.requirement: the register's `## Branches` section holds at least one branch row, or the single line `Branches: none -- <why>` with a reason (never both, never neither)
never_empty.why: a branch of a requirement is a row with an id, and an empty list that nobody declared empty is how a qualifier of the story disappears without a trace; the empty outcome of the section is its declared `none` with the reason a person can read

never_empty.requirement: the register's `## Source obligations` section homes every unit of the story's text; it is legitimately absent only when the ticket has 0 units
never_empty.why: every sentence of the story and of its kept linked tickets needs a home (a requirement, a branch, a named non-obligation, a named exclusion or a named remainder), so the empty outcome of the section is a ticket with no unit, which the detector says in words (`0 units in the ticket`)

never_empty.requirement: the register's `## Attachments` section holds one row per file whose bytes were read (or one `rest` row with a reason); it is legitimately absent when the story and its kept tickets have no such file
never_empty.why: a file is what the role looks at after the matrix, and a file nobody compared with the requirements is how a document or a UI that contradicts them goes unseen; the empty outcome of the section is a story with no file, which needs no section and no `none` line

never_empty.requirement: one row per draft the person answered about at gate B, and the one row `gate_b` (state `nothing_chosen`) when the person chose no draft
never_empty.why: the reporter is dispatched when gate B ordered bugs or quarantined a test, and `--bugs ordered` with no draft chosen is a legal decision (controller.py gate-decision); the legal empty outcome is therefore a row of its own, never an empty list, so `scope` is never empty and `filed: []` is stated beside it
never_empty.guard: no guard: handoff_check.py::check refuses the empty list (`no rows`), which is the intended outcome; the role's empty-decision door is the `gate_b` row the contract names, and its other door is `blocked` and handoff_help.py

never_empty.requirement: one row per requirement of the register under review (or the artifact name)
never_empty.why: the stage critic reviews a register that holds at least one R row (NE2, NE19), so a review with no scope row has looked at nothing; the legal way to say a place was not looked at is `not_looked`, never an empty scope
never_empty.guard: no guard: handoff_check.py::check refuses the empty list (`no rows`), which is the intended outcome; the role's door is `blocked` and handoff_help.py

never_empty.requirement: one row per plan row or requirement under review
never_empty.why: the stage critic reviews a plan that exists only when S3 produced rows (an empty S3 plan is the open-questions halt, not a result), so a review with no scope row has looked at nothing; the legal way to say a place was not looked at is `not_looked`, never an empty scope
never_empty.guard: no guard: handoff_check.py::check refuses the empty list (`no rows`), which is the intended outcome; the role's door is `blocked` and handoff_help.py

never_empty.requirement: a story with a non-real side states its assumptions as `provisional: []` when it assumes nothing, a story with every side real carries no `provisional` key, and a test row without `provisional` reads as `[]`
never_empty.why: the registry of assumptions is read by one reader, and an absent field is never read as a malformed one: a manifest written before the registry existed carries neither field, and an empty list sent is the declared empty outcome

never_empty.requirement: a first look that was walked holds one row per requirement of the register (a requirement the stand does not show is a `missing` row, never an absent one); a first look that was not walked is `null: <reason>` with `rows: []` and one gap line, and an empty register is the reason `empty_register`, never an empty walk
never_empty.why: an absent row would read as 'nothing wrong' and a requirement would drop out of the first look without a trace; the empty outcomes are declared in the record itself (`null` with a reason from references/first-look-statuses.json, `rows: []`, a gap line), and `first_look.put` refuses a record that leaves a requirement out

never_empty.requirement: the S1 reference window of a story whose side has a reference writes the snapshot; a window that saw nothing (the old version could not be reached, or nothing of it was walked) is `items: []` with one gap line saying why, never an absent file and never an empty list with no reason; a story with no reference has no snapshot and nothing reads one
never_empty.why: an absent snapshot would read as 'the old version does nothing' and a parity requirement would lose its expected value without a trace; the empty outcome is declared in the record itself (`items: []`, a gap line) and `reference_snapshot.put` refuses an empty list with no gap line
